query: Broadcom custom AI accelerator XPU revenue growth
normalized: accelerator ai broadcom custom growth revenue xpu

output.content:
Broadcom does **not** publicly disclose a standalone revenue line for custom AI accelerators (“XPUs”); it reports the broader **AI semiconductor revenue** category, which includes custom accelerators and AI networking. [[1]] 

The reported AI-semiconductor trajectory is exceptionally steep: **$8.4 billion in FY2026 Q1** (+106% YoY), **$10.8 billion in Q2** (+143% YoY), and **$16.7 billion in Q3** (+221% YoY and +54% sequentially). [[2]] [[3]] [[1]] 

For **FY2026 Q4**, Broadcom guided to **$21.7 billion** of AI-semiconductor revenue, implying **236% year-over-year growth**; management explicitly attributed the momentum to continued strong demand for custom AI accelerators and networking. [[1]] 

For context, AI-semiconductor revenue was **$6.5 billion in FY2025 Q4**, up 74% year over year, while Broadcom expected **$8.2 billion in FY2026 Q1**, driven by custom AI accelerators and Ethernet AI switches. [[4]] 

Thus, using the company’s combined AI-semiconductor measure as the closest disclosed proxy, revenue expanded from **$6.5 billion in FY2025 Q4 to $16.7 billion in FY2026 Q3**—about **2.6× in three quarters**—with the Q4 FY2026 outlook indicating a further step-up to **$21.7 billion**. [[4]] [[1]] 

The principal caveat is that this is **not XPU-only growth**: Broadcom’s disclosed category also captures AI networking, so the exact dollar contribution and growth rate of custom accelerators alone cannot be derived from its reported financials. [[1]]
